title: Private View at the Void Gallery
teaser: At the opening of Yan Levanevsky's exhibition, guests spent half an hour photographing his new piece, a glass cube with a motionless figure inside, and marvelling at how lifelike it was. The figure turned out to be Levanevsky himself. Now the police have hundreds of photos from the private view, and in one of them the killer may be standing right by the cube with a glass in hand. The gallery doors are shut.
locations: The smoking area in the courtyard

habits.label: Paint under the nails
habits.habit: Dried oil paint under their nails
clues: The glass of the cube in the main hall has a smear of fresh ultramarine, and Levanevsky used no blue in this exhibition. The culprit has paint under their nails.
The stem of a glass in the champagne bar has traces of oil paint. The culprit has paint under their nails.

habits.label: Smells of turpentine
clues: By the cube in the main hall a sharp smell of turpentine cuts through the perfume and champagne. The culprit smells of turpentine.
The armchair in the gallerist's office smells of turpentine, though there's no paint in there. The culprit smells of turpentine.

habits.label: Black beret
clues: The main hall camera shows a shadow behind the cube with a flat round top, like a beret. The culprit wears a beret.
A black beret lies in a puddle in the courtyard smoking area, and nobody will say it's theirs. The culprit wears a beret.

habits.label: Glass in hand
habits.habit: Hasn't let go of a glass of champagne all evening
clues: There are drops of champagne on the floor inside the cube. The culprit has had a glass of champagne in hand all evening.
A half-finished glass from the bar stands on a shelf in the picture store. The culprit has had a glass of champagne in hand all evening.

habits.label: Black polo neck
clues: There's a black knitted fibre on the glass of the cube in the main hall. The culprit wears a black polo neck.
A black thread, like from a polo neck, is caught on a frame in the artist's studio. The culprit wears a black polo neck.

habits.label: Platinum bob
clues: Levanevsky is clutching a short, straight, platinum hair. The culprit has a platinum bob.
There's a light hair dyed almost white on the back of the armchair in the gallerist's office. The culprit has a platinum bob.

habits.label: Red glasses
clues: A red plastic chip from a pair of frames lies under the cube in the main hall. The culprit wears red-framed glasses.
A red arm from a pair of glasses lies on the table in the restoration room. The culprit wears red-framed glasses.

habits.label: Silk scarf
habits.habit: A silk scarf round the neck
clues: Levanevsky's neck shows marks of smooth fabric: he was strangled with something silk. The culprit wears a silk scarf.
A bright silk scarf tied in a knot was left on the bench in the courtyard smoking area. The culprit wears a silk scarf.

habits.label: Catalogue under the arm
habits.habit: Never parts with the exhibition catalogue
clues: An exhibition catalogue lies in the cube next to Levanevsky, folded open at the page about this very piece. The culprit carries the exhibition catalogue.
A page torn out of the catalogue lies in the loading passage of the picture store. The culprit carries the exhibition catalogue.

habits.label: Charcoal behind the ear
habits.habit: A charcoal pencil tucked behind their ear
clues: The label by the cube in the main hall has a black charcoal line on it, as if someone tried to write something. The culprit has a charcoal pencil behind their ear.
A broken charcoal pencil lies on the floor of the artist's studio. The culprit has a charcoal pencil behind their ear.

habits.label: Single earring
habits.habit: A long earring in one ear
clues: A single long earring with a stone is stuck under the cube in the main hall. The culprit wears an earring in one ear.
In the champagne bar the waiter found an earring back on a tray. The culprit wears an earring in one ear.

habits.label: Clay on the hands
clues: The door of the cube in the main hall has grey fingerprints in clay. The culprit has clay on their hands.
The sink in the artist's studio has streaks of grey clay. The culprit has clay on their hands.

habits.label: Silver-topped cane
clues: The parquet by the cube in the main hall has round dents from the tip of a cane. The culprit walks with a cane.
The picture store door has a scratch, like from a silver cane handle. The culprit walks with a cane.

habits.label: Letters on the fingers
clues: Before he died, Levanevsky scratched a few letters on the glass, apparently the ones he saw on someone's fingers. The culprit has letters on their fingers.
The exhibition photographer caught a hand holding a glass at the bar, and there are letters across its knuckles. The culprit has letters on their fingers.

habits.label: Oud perfume
clues: Inside the cube there's a thick smell of wood and resin, like oud perfume. The culprit wears oud perfume.
The restoration room, which usually smells of nothing, has a waft of heavy woody perfume. The culprit wears oud perfume.

habits.label: Coat over the shoulders
habits.habit: Wears a coat thrown over their shoulders
clues: In the main hall footage a figure in a coat with empty sleeves flickers behind the cube. The culprit wears a coat over their shoulders.
A button from a long coat hangs on a branch in the courtyard smoking area. The culprit wears a coat over their shoulders.

cash: The cube's sale was signed off half an hour before the opening, but the money didn't go to the gallery's account. The culprit had access to money.
All of the evening's takings are gone from the bar till, and the log says "spent on the artist". The culprit had access to money.
safe: The safe in the gallerist's office was opened with the code, and Levanevsky's contracts with buyers are missing from it. The culprit knows the safe combination.
The combination cabinet in the restoration room is open, and the folder with the paintings' authentication reports is gone. The culprit knows the safe combination.
sched: The plan was to open the cube for ten minutes before the private view, and during those minutes nobody was in the main hall. The culprit knows the schedule.
At 21:40 the guard does his round of the picture store, and he was away from the main hall for exactly seven minutes. The culprit knows the schedule.
french: On the label by the cube someone has written over the title "Nature morte", French for "still life", literally "dead nature". The culprit knows French.
"Imposteur", French for "Impostor", is written in charcoal on a canvas in the artist's studio. The culprit knows French.
quiet: The parquet in the main hall clicks under heels, yet in the hush before the private view nobody heard a thing. The culprit moves silently.
The waiter stood by the picture store door and insists nobody went in. The culprit moves silently.
driver: The shipper's van was moved from the service entrance to the courtyard smoking area, and its engine is still warm. The culprit can drive.
The collector's car was driven into the next courtyard, though he gave his keys to the cloakroom attendant. The culprit can drive.
tools: The door of the cube was opened by taking off a hinge with an Allen key, then put back perfectly. The culprit is handy with tools.
A painting in the store was taken out of its frame without damaging a single nail. The culprit is handy with tools.
passages: A door behind a false wall leads from the restoration room into the main hall. Only the installers know about it, and the wall has been pushed aside. The culprit knows the service passages.
A loading ramp leads from the picture store into the courtyard, and there are fresh footprints on it. The culprit knows the service passages.
strong: Levanevsky was seated inside the cube as if posing, and that isn't easy with a limp body. The culprit is physically strong.
The glass wall of the cube, which usually takes two people to lift, was raised and set back in place. The culprit is physically strong.
medic: Levanevsky's glass held traces of a muscle relaxant that leaves a person unable to move. The culprit knows about poisons.
Someone poured off a solvent from a bottle in the restoration room that puts people to sleep in small doses. The culprit knows about poisons.
keys: The artist's studio was locked, and two canvases are missing from it. The culprit had keys.
The picture store is locked, but one of Levanevsky's works is no longer there. The culprit had keys.
tech: Ten minutes before the opening the main hall camera was turned to face the wall through the app. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
The cube's lighting was reset so that the face inside can't be seen. The culprit knows their way around machinery.
